title: Nutraceuticals, Functional Foods and Junk Foods
shortDescription: Health-promoting foods and supplements and the regulatory framework; contrast with HFSS junk foods.
genZNote: Nutraceuticals are food-as-medicine with a legal caveat; junk food is the 'food-like product' that gave us HFSS. Know the line between them.

sections.heading: Definitions
sections.body: Indian framework: FSS (Health Supplements, Nutraceuticals, Food for Special Dietary Use, Food for Special Medical Purpose, Functional Food and Novel Food) Regulations, 2016; Advertising and Claims Regulations, 2018 control health claims.

table.caption: Terms
rows: Food or part of food with medical or health benefit (term coined by Stephen DeFelice, 1989)
Food offering benefits beyond basic nutrition, usually in a food form
Probiotic yoghurt, oats with β-glucan, fortified juices
Live microbes / substrate for them / combination

sections.heading: Bioactive Compounds
bullets: Polyphenols and flavonoids (antioxidants); carotenoids (lycopene, lutein); glucosinolates; phytosterols (cholesterol lowering); omega-3 fatty acids; dietary fibre/β-glucan; probiotics; peptides.
Evidence: health claims must be scientifically substantiated; "cure" claims are prohibited.

sections.heading: Junk Foods (HFSS)
bullets: High in fat, sugar and salt and low in micronutrients/fibre: chips, sugary beverages, confectionery, instant noodles, fast-food items.
Health links: obesity, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, dental caries, NAFLD.

Policy: FSSAI regulation on safe food and balanced diets for children in schools (restricting HFSS foods in school canteens and within about 50 m of schools), front-of-pack labelling proposals, trans-fat limits, Eat Right India messages on reducing fat, sugar and salt.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Nutraceuticals and functional foods deliver health benefits beyond basic nutrition under specific regulations, while junk foods are energy-dense, nutrient-poor products linked to chronic disease.

commonTraps: Do not equate supplements with medicines.
